summary_paragraph: A 59-year-old woman with advanced HIV (CD4 41, off HAART) and end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis was admitted for a right femoral dialysis catheter infection with purulent drainage and hypotension. The infected catheter was removed, and she was treated with a seven-day course of vancomycin. A new tunneled catheter was successfully placed on the left side after an initial failed attempt. Imaging raised concern for an IVC thrombus, prompting a brief course of heparin, but a subsequent CT confirmed no clot, and anticoagulation was discontinued. She was asymptomatic throughout, with stable vital signs and no bacteremia. During admission, she was treated for presumed oral candidiasis, and her medications were adjusted, including increasing aspirin to 325 mg daily due to prior atrial fibrillation, starting Nephrocaps, and modifying phosphate binders. Her mood was depressed, and social work follow-up was arranged. She improved clinically and was discharged home with plans for ongoing outpatient care.
